problem: The sentence 'Differentiating with respect to T at constant pressure removes the direct part and leaves the standard enthalpy' is too vague; a student cannot see how the derivative of ln K gives ΔH°.
fix: Show the step: start from ln K = −ΔG°/(RT) and use the Gibbs–Helmholtz relation d(ΔG°/T)/dT = −ΔH°/T²; this gives d ln K/dT = ΔH°/(RT²).

problem: 'The derivative is local: it gives the slope of ln K at one temperature' does not say slope against which variable, so it can be confused with the slope of the ln K versus 1/T plot.
fix: Say: 'The derivative is local: it gives d ln K/dT at one temperature. On a plot of ln K against 1/T, the slope is −ΔH°/R.'

problem: The answer defines the symbols but does not give the units of ΔH° or the value and units of R, so a student cannot use the equation numerically.
fix: Add: 'ΔH° is in J/mol and R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.'

problem: The answer says a straight line in ln K versus 1/T follows from constant ΔH° alone, but the intercept also requires ΔS° to be constant, i.e. ΔCp° ≈ 0.
fix: Add that the plot is straight only when both ΔH° and ΔS° are nearly constant (ΔCp° ≈ 0); then slope = −ΔH°/R and intercept = ΔS°/R.
